10.1016_j.electacta.2026.149048: A thin film combinatorial library with a compositional spread from 0.5 to 15 at.% Dy in Al is produced by thermal co-evaporation and analyzed via energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, inductively coupled plasma - optical emission spectroscopy, nanoindentation, and several electrochemical measurements. The morphological analysis indicate grain refinement upon additional Dy in the alloy until amorphization around 7 at.% Dy in Al. The crystallographic analysis reveal an amorphization of the alloys by the broadening of the XRD peaks which starts from 3 at.% Dy. The grain refinement results in an increase in hardness and Young modulus until 7 at.% Dy then the values decline upon additional Dy. Electrochemical studies reveal an overall increase of the oxide film formation factor during anodization and of the dielectric permittivity with rising Dy content. Furthermore, alloys with higher Dy ratios have a lower corrosion potential and a higher corrosion rate. This is confirmed by optical emission spectroscopy of the electrolytes used which show much higher dissolution of Dy.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.156277: Conductive hydrogels are widely applied in bioelectronics, sensors, and energy systems due to their flexibility, porosity, and ionic conductivity. However, their electrical properties strongly depend on composition and testing conditions. This study investigates the electrical stability of pure and particle-loaded poly (N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) hydrogels prepared using different solvent systems (water, 1.3 wt% and 3 – 4 wt.% poly (3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly (styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS)). Measurements were performed in a controlled two-electrode configuration to ensure controlled testing conditions and reproducibility. The effects of working medium (water or 0.1 M KOH), conductive filler (carbon black), and solvent composition on ionic and electronic conductivity were systematically evaluated. Repeated soaking led to significant changes in impedance, which correlated with morphological evolution observed by SEM. The results demonstrate that the electrical response of conductive hydrogels is highly sensitive to composition and processing history, emphasizing the need for consistent experimental conditions in their characterization.
10.1021_acsnano.5c20908: Electrocatalytic platinum nanomaterials are promising for tumor therapy, but their efficiency is constrained by the spatial limitations inherent in the traditional electrode/electrolyte three-phase interface mechanism. This study develops an injectable composite conductive hydrogel comprising sodium alginate, gelatin@polypyrrole, Pt nanowires, and Pt nanoparticles (SA/Gel@PPy/Pt NWs/Pt NPs) to overcome this issue. By synergizing the embedded Gel@PPy/Pt NWs with the Pt wire electrode, we create a 3D continuous electron circuit throughout the hydrogel. This overcomes the spatial limits of traditional interfaces, expanding the electrocatalytic chlorine evolution reaction from the 2D electrode surface into the 3D hydrogel volume, thus constructing a bulk-phase continuous electrode. This electrode integrates discrete catalytic sites via nanoscale electron pathways, rather than relying on the monolithic scaffold of traditional porous electrodes. The hydrogel leverages endogenous chloride ions to sustain electrocatalytic hypochlorous acid (HClO) generation, while its excellent tissue conformability enhances the therapeutic effect, enabling highly localized therapy. This potent oxidant (HClO) acts dually: it triggers proinflammatory antitumor immunity and dissolves the platinum components to release Pt ions, which synergistically induce DNA damage and enhance immunogenic cell death (ICD). Consequently, animal experiments demonstrated significant tumor suppression in a mouse model, establishing this 3D nanoelectrode network as a paradigm for efficient electrocatalytic tumor therapy.
